# How AI is Changing Content Marketing in 2025

[Core dna team](#author-details)

January 29, 2025 - (10 min read)

[Content Marketing](/blogs/categories/content-marketing) | [Digital Marketing](/blogs/categories/digital-marketing) | [Strategy](/blogs/categories/growth-strategy)

Content is king, as the saying goes. And we’re glad to report that the long reign of the king is set to continue well into 2025.

Since the internet first evolved, and even way before that — with the likes of mail catalogs, out of home advertisements, and brochures — businesses have used content to get their message across.

And in 2025, content remains the cornerstone by which many are measuring their success. 

You don't have a brand without a great online presence, and many businesses are looking at how to increase their content marketing to stay competitive as AI content becomes more and more common.

In this article, we're delving into the murky world of **content Marketing in 2025**. We're going to look at Generative AI content creation, the strategies you can use to make the most of AI content, and actionable recommendations to increase your ROI from your current marketing efforts.

Then we're going to conclude by taking a look at how Core dna can help you reach your content marketing goals. Let’s get stuck in!

**In hurry? Get our Trends Guide**

#### On this page:

Where were you back in 2022 when ChatGPT stormed onto the scene? Were you in business, in tech, or even in a content creation role?

For those of us that were content marketers, ChatGPT took our industry by storm. It's hard now to look back and think how we made content without AI content creation tools giving us a little push when we need it. But at the time, ChatGPT was, without a doubt, revolutionary.

AI-content is so ubiquitous, you’ll almost certainly have clicked on an AI-generated blog post, watched an AI generated video, or received an AI generated email. But the question is, what does this mean for **content marketing in 2025?**

Let’s take a look at how AI is making waves, three years on.

### AI Content Creation

From simple blogging to video creation and photo editing. AI tools should be introduced in every step of your content creation. Not only does it make youmore efficient, it also helps you 10X your productivity.

You are probably already familiar with Generative AI bots like ChatGPT and Jasper AI, which answer our prompts to analyze trending topics, search queries, and audience behavior.

These tools spit out content ideas in seconds, then with the right prompts you can work with them to transform ideas into full length blog posts, social media graphics, white papers, and even websites. - This article have more than [35 SEO prompts](https://team-gpt.com/blog/chatgpt-prompts-for-seo/) to help you generate content.

These tools are making [content creation](/blogs/best-types-of-content)easy, but beware! If you are using these tools to generate ideas, the chances are your competitors are too. That might mean that your content gets sucked into the blur of similar content online. You might need a human to proofread your ideas, before they get into production.

**Our top tip for AI SEO blog writing?** The secret here is to do research. Before you use your AI SEO blog writing prompt, start by using a prompt to research the SERP results for the keyword you are trying to rank for.

You can use ask ChatGPT or whatever ai tools you use with access to the web to analyze the top 10 results and create your article outline based on that. You can even use it to research all the related keyword and the frequency each one should be use within your content.

If you are generating the content with AI as well, make sure you include proprietary information or unique content so that the readers have some value out of your article and blog.

Don't blindly post your article, make sure that you read it and that it provides valuable information for the reader not just content that ranks. Our SEO guru told us to always put the content through this question:  **"if you a google engineer was looking over your shoulder, would you still post it."**

Also as google cracks down on AI generated content, make sure your content can pass the test by using tools like [originality.ai.](https://originality.ai/)

**Check out this video for more tips on how to speed up content and video creation with AI.**

### Personalization at Scale

But it isn't just in content generation where AI shines. Some of the most innovative ways AI is being integrated into a [**content marketing strategy**](/blogs/content-marketing-tips-content-type-ideas) is in how it allows businesses to completely personalize the way their content is presented to their users.

Let's take an example. Imagine a travel company offering unique trip options based on the country their visitor is resident in. Or imagine a fashion company showcasing its products on models with your body type, so you can really imagine what those clothes look like.

All these are ways AI is being used to personalize content experiences.

In our recent article about the [2025 eCommerce trends](/blogs/ecommerce-trends-2025), we can see that AI is really transforming the way brands interact with their customers. If A/B testing was once the rule of optimization, **Generative AI** has enabled hyper-personalization which take it to another level.

 Brands can really get granular when segmenting their database and let AI determine which option to show depending on the results customer profile.

How is that different? So if before option B won, then that is the one that would be shown to everyone. But that info only got us a general results what is yes option B won but for the group female, 30 to 40 years old option A was actually more popular?

Before AI, getting this detailed would require a lot of time. Today, **generative AI tools** can do the job for us and actually always show the best options for the segment.

Get deeper into this by checking out [Klaviyo AI](https://www.klaviyo.com/features/ai). Integrating Klaviyo with your [eCommerce platform](/blogs/best-ecommerce-platform) give you powerful tools to enhance personalization.

For businesses looking to experiment with this new type of content, tools like Dynamic Yield or HubSpot help you segment audiences and personalize content across all your touchpoints, making use of your data in new, exciting ways.

### Predictive Analytics for Better Decisions

Got data? If so, you can start to use AI and even more innovative ways. For example, AI can analyze all your historical data to predict how your content will perform in the future. With dynamic scheduling, you can post new content pieces at precisely the right moment to get seen by the most people.

To do this, use tools like Google Analytics 4 to refine and tweak your publishing schedules and content formats for best results.

**Understand how a DXP and CMS impact your online presence and content creation. Get out guide:**  [Digital Experience Platform (DXP) vs CMS](/guides/dxp-vs-cms-explained)

## AI tools for Multi-Format Content Creation

The world of **Generative AI** is expanding across multiple different content formats. Video, audio output, graphics, infographics, and even design, are all things that AI can take off your plate. Let’s take take a deeper look at how it impact marketing content creation.

### **AI SEO tools**

Writing blogs is all about improving SEO rankings. And that doesn't just happen by accident. Instead you need a reliable content calendar packed with keyword optimized blocks that move the needle when it comes to your traffic.

In the past, writing SEO optimized blogs was complicated. You’d need an expert blog writer to help you with the correct format, internal linking strategy, and keyword approach that you should take.

But now? All you need is a few AI in SEO tools.

[**SurferSEO:**](https://surferseo.com/category/seo-writing/)A comprehensive suite of tools that can help you create content from scratch, analyze your competitors, identify opportunities for improvement

[**Writesonic**](https://writesonic.com/ai-article-writer-generator)**:**Some say Writesonic is an even better writer than ChatGPT. We will let you judge by testing the same prompt on both.

[**Neuron Writer:**](https://neuronwriter.com/)In the same way has surfer SEO, neuron writer help you keep track of the keywords in your article and write super optimized SEO content for Search engine.

For example, you could write a blog using SurferSEO’s AI credits that would analyse the SERPs, provide keyword examples, FAQs, images, and even alt text! All you’d need to do is proofread and get it live… a far cry from the lengthy blog writing processes of old.

### **AI Video tools**

One great SEO trick is to include video content on your pages. But creating video content is time consuming, with lengthy requirements for filming, costly recording studio invoices, and time consuming script writing processes.

If only there were an AI tool that could do it all for you! Well, the good news is, here are a few tools that can help you create video content without a camera crew.

[**HeyGen**:](https://www.heygen.com/create-avatar-video) If you have a camera-shy team and no budget for professional video crew, HeyGen is your tool. With super realistic AI avatar, it can create human like video in more than 175 language.

[**Pictory**:](https://app.pictory.ai/home) If you have an idea but not sure how to translate it to video, try Pictory. It creates videos out of text, ppt or even images so simply type your idea and let the magic happen.

[**Veed**:](https://www.veed.io/use-cases/marketing-social-media) Is a video editing tool on autopilot. It is an all in one tool that is really popular when it comes to using generative AI to create videos. With AI voiceover, subtitles, avatars and much more.

[**Revid.ai:**](https://www.revid.ai/tools) Create social shorts in minutes from ideation to publishing using Revid. It is a suite of 20+ AI video tools that you can use with a few clicks.

Now, there's no need to overcome your stage fright. instead you can get an AI Avatar to present that podcast for you!

You can even use AI content creation tools to streamline the editing process, add closed captions for accessibility, edit and snip to remove background noise, and even touch up your makeup.

Not sure how this would work?

Imagine an ecom brand taking their existing images of products and converting them into conversion-oriented videos using AI content creation tools.

Or imagine a podcaster transforming a photo of themselves into an AI video avatar that can flawlessly present an entire online course or webinar—without the podcaster even in attendance! It’s all possible in 2025.

### **AI tools for Graphic Design**

Bored of the same old stock photos? So are we. More importantly, so are your customers.

But with AI-powered marketing tools, you can create engaging, exciting, interesting, eye-catching graphics all at the touch of a button. Imagine turning a blog post into an infographic design to easily communicate to your audience. Imagine creating photos of anything you can dream of from a simple AI prompt.

This is the power of AI design tools like:

[**C**](https://www.canva.com/magic-design/)[**anva's AI**](https://www.canva.com/magic-design/): Canva added great AI features to their platform. From magic eraser to text to image creation, it can be used by anyone to upgrade your visuals.

[**DALL-E 3**](https://openart.ai/): You can use chatgpt to create images using DALL-E 3. While it is still not perfect t can help in creative briefs to illustrate what you are trying to achieve.

[**Adobe Firefly**:](https://www.adobe.com/ai/overview.html) Of course the most used suite by creative has now integrated AI to all its tools to enhance the experience and superpower the creatives.

[**Midjourney**:](https://www.midjourney.com/home)If you haven't seen a mid journey image yet, let me tell you it is impressive. While midjourney needs more advanced skills the possibilities are endless and the quality is just brilliant.

AI tools like these help marketers create visually appealing graphics, without getting on the phone to that expensive graphic designer. All the better for making content that catches the eye of your reader, without breaking the bank or dragging out the timeline.

## Supercharged SEO with AI

We’ve seen graphic design, podcasts, and endless blogs all generated with AI. But when it comes to AI-powered marketing, using it for improving SEO rankings is probably one of the best ways.

For brands aiming to improve visibility and maximize returns on their content, AI provides an edge that’s hard to ignore.

Let's dive into why… and how you can put it to good use.

### **Smarter Keyword Research**

With Generative AI capabilities being integrated in tools like **SEMrush**and **Ahrefs,**the process of keyword research has changed. 

Instead of hours spent manually analyzing search terms (who else remembers those long hours staring down Google Trends?!), these tools uncover trends and surface opportunities for long-tail keywords that might otherwise be overlooked. And the best part? You can do it in seconds.

Truly, it’s impossible to imagine an SEO-world without AI for keyword research — and tools like these tell us why.

### **Refining Content**

But, as any content marketer worth their salt can tell you, content that performs well in search isn’t just about throwing in the right keywords, no matter what tool you used to find them. 

AI platforms like SurferSEO and MarketMuse help marketers understand all the complex, intriguing, difficult nuances of optimization, whether that looks like improving headings and meta descriptions to strengthening internal link structures. 

### **Voice Search and Conversational Queries**

Welcome to the new age!... And is that voice search on the horizon?

SEO isn’t so stuck to us typing in our keywords any more. Now, people might be turning to new ways to search, including by voice recognition. And that brings with it some challenges.

AI is making it easier to bridge the gap between written content and audio content that can answer all these queries. Tools like BrightEdge are truly at the forefront of this shift, meaning that brands like yours can stay relevant in a world that might be driven by voice commands.

### **Competitor Analysis**

Understanding what competitors are doing has always been essential, but AI takes it a step further. Platforms like SimilarWeb and Crayon provide a deep dive into competitor strategies, highlighting opportunities they’ve missed. 

For instance, if a competitor hasn’t addressed a specific topic cluster, it becomes an opening to capture a new audience. This level of insight allows marketers to approach gaps strategically and create content that fills those voids.

## How Your CMS Platform Can Help You Achieve Your Content Marketing Goals in 2025

Creating compelling content is only one part of a successful content marketing strategy. Delivering the right content to the right people at the right time is what will determine success. This is where a [content management system (CMS)](https://www.coredna.com/blogs/how-to-choose-a-cms)that is adaptable, intelligent, and scalable can make the difference. 

#### **1. Seamless AI Integration for Content Creation**

Content marketing is increasingly reliant on AI tools for content creation. Having a CMS platform that integrate smoothly with AI technologies is essential. At Core dna we are working to shape the future of AI for content marketers with integrative AI and SEO tools but also by creating an integration ecosystem that is flexible and a [composable architecture](https://www.coredna.com/blogs/composable-commerce). 

By leveraging AI and your CMS platform together, you can streamline your content creation process, cut down on production time, and maintain a consistent flow of high-quality content that resonates with your target audience.

#### **2. Personalization at Scale**

We know personalization is the future of brands no matter what your industry is. With AI, businesses of all sizes can create personalized experience across all channels. 

Your CMS platform should empower you to deliver hyper-personalized experiences at scale, tailoring content to different customer segments based on their preferences, behaviors, and demographics. 

By analyzing customer data, your CMS can dynamically adjust content for individual users, ensuring that every touchpoint feels relevant and engaging, whether it’s on your website, through email campaigns, or within mobile apps.

#### **3. Predictive Content Performance with Analytics**

Your CMS platform should be equipped with powerful analytics tools that help you predict how your content will perform. By integrating predictive analytics into your CMS, you can use historical data to optimize your content strategies and ensure your content reaches the right audience at the right time. 

Want to know the best times to post? Or which topics are trending in your niche? With your CMS, these insights can be automated, making your marketing efforts more effective and data-driven.

This can be especially useful in an era where timing and context are everything. Your CMS can [help schedule posts and content releases](/blogs/case-study-adotg) when they are most likely to engage your audience, ensuring you stay ahead of the competition.

#### **4. Optimized Omnichannel Content Delivery**

Consumer expect to have similar brand experience across all devices and locations. Your content management system should offer headless capabilties allowing you to deploy content across multiple touchpoints with ease.

This multichannel capability also means that you can have one central content hub feeding into multiple micro sites, landing pages and marketplaces. It ensures brand consistency and that your content is always where your audience. With AI integrated into your CMS, it can even help optimize content specifically for each medium.

#### **5. Streamlined Content Workflows and Collaboration**

As your content team grows, so does the need for collaboration. An [enterprise content management system s](/blogs/10-best-enterprise-cms-of-2025-choosing-the-right-enterprise-cms)hould make it easy for teams to work together, whether they're on the ground or spread across the globe. 

From content planning to creation to publishing, your CMS should simplify workflows, making it easier to coordinate efforts, track progress, and ensure that everyone is aligned on strategy.

By automating repetitive tasks like scheduling posts or approving content, your team can focus more on strategic work and less on time-consuming manual processes. Plus, the CMS should allow for easy version control and feedback loops, so you can ensure your content meets quality standards before it’s published.

#### **6. Scalability for Future Growth**

No matter what industry your are in or content you create, the most important factors when choosing a CMS in 2025 is its ability to scale with your business. As your content marketing efforts grow, your CMS should be able to handle an increasing volume of content without sacrificing performance. 

As you expand into new markets or diversify your content offerings, a scalable CMS can accommodate your evolving needs and ensure your content marketing strategy continues to thrive.

## Predicting 2025 Content Marketing Trends

And with all this  going on, how can businesses look ahead to the future? Well, one big way they can make an impact is by staying ahead of the trends.

And to do that? Why not use AI?

AI is great at identifying topics or keywords likely to gain traction in the future, recognizing the patters that us humans are likely to miss

A content marketer might discover, for example, that interest in “[hyper-personalized AI marketing”](https://www.coredna.com/blogs/trends-embracing-predictive-personalized-marketing-in-ecommerce) is on the rise and get ahead by creating content around it. This hyper-predictive ability means that content always hits on what people are searching for and looking for – and AI can help you get there!

# 50+ Content Marketing Statistics to Watch in 2025

Akshita Sharma · Content Marketing Associate

June 20th, 2025 · 24 min read

Remember when a blog post and some Facebook updates counted as a complete content strategy?

Those days are long gone.

Podcasts command massive audiences. Short-form video dominates feeds. And if your content isn’t optimized for AI overviews or voice search, you’re already behind.

Today's audiences expect content that meets them exactly where they are — delivering the right message, at the right moment, through their preferred channels. The brands winning right now are the ones using these insights to guide their decisions.

If you're interested in learning about what's new in content marketing, this post will provide you with 50+ valuable content marketing statistics that matter most for your content marketing strategy in 2025.

## **Content marketing statistics to shape your strategy in 2025**

### **1. AI content marketing statistics**

Businesses everywhere are stepping up their marketing game, and AI content marketing tools are leading the charge. Here's something that might surprise you: over [80% of marketers](https://www.statista.com/statistics/1293758/ai-marketing-revenue-worldwide/) around the world are already using AI in their digital marketing strategies. That's huge.

Why the sudden rush to AI? Simple. These tools deliver both efficiency and creativity that traditional methods just can't match.

Take Typeface, for example. We’re an enterprise-grade generative AI platform that is changing how marketing teams work. The platform reimagines every step of the content creation process with specialized AI marketing agents (or [Arc Agents](/product/arc-agents)) for campaign ideation, content creation, channel optimization.

It also comes with [Brand Hub](/product/brand-hub), a unique brand intelligence system that captures everything about your brand, from assets and audiences to visual aesthetics and voices, turning static guidelines into a dynamic, living system. This innovative approach allows for deep searches, scalable personalization, and proactive brand governance[.](/product/arc-agents)

Here's a look at some content marketing statistics that reveal how AI is reshaping the strategies marketers employ:

* Over 74% of marketers think that most people will be using AI in their workplaces by 2030 ([HubSpot State of AI Report 2024](https://blog.hubspot.com/marketing/state-of-ai-report)).

* 43% of marketers using AI tools use it for content creation ([HubSpot State of AI Report 2024](https://blog.hubspot.com/marketing/state-of-ai-report?__hstc=162473507.e4916d85d797cce23c21afed017f8f11.1732083461628.1747889100805.1747902254414.330&__hssc=162473507.1.1747902254414&__hsfp=4051365776)). 74.2% of new webpages include content generated by AI ([Ahrefs](https://ahrefs.com/blog/ai-marketing-statistics/)).

* Nearly 20% of marketers allocate over 40% of their marketing budgets to AI-powered content marketing campaigns ([Influencer Marketing Hub AI Marketing Report 2024](https://influencermarketinghub.com/ai-marketing-benchmark-report/)). As AI technology advances, more marketers are likely to see the value of these tools in reaching their marketing objectives, leading to increased AI budget allocations.

* 86% of marketers have reported that AI saved them over an hour each day in coming up with creative ideas for content ([HubSpot State of AI Report 2024](https://blog.hubspot.com/marketing/state-of-ai-report)).

* Nearly half of AI users (49%) create multi-step, complex [AI writing prompts](/blog/ai-writing-prompts-to-create-content-faster) for content generation ([Semrush AI Content Marketing Report 2024](https://www.semrush.com/contentshake/ai-content-marketing-report/)). Complex prompts help users guide AI more precisely, ensuring the results match their goals and vision. Alternatively, you can use Typeface's Magic Prompt feature, which automatically enhances [AI image prompts](/education/typeface-academy/how-to-write-good-ai-image-prompts) with modifiers to optimize the images.

* A strong confidence in AI's capabilities is reflected by the fact that 70.6% of marketers feel that AI tools can outperform humans in essential marketing tasks. ([Influencer Marketing Hub AI Marketing Report 2024](https://influencermarketinghub.com/ai-marketing-benchmark-report/)). At Typeface, we believe the best content is produced via human-AI collaboration. AI increases the speed and volume of generating great first drafts that are 80-90% complete, giving people the time and space to add human intelligence and editing to get it to the finish line.

* More than 40% of marketers use AI for learning how to do things while 34% use it for research and another 34% for brainstorming ([HubSpot State of AI Report 2024](https://blog.hubspot.com/marketing/state-of-ai-report)).

[Source](https://blog.hubspot.com/marketing/state-of-ai-report)

* 86% of marketers who use AI spend time editing the content it generates ([HubSpot State of AI Report 2024)](https://blog.hubspot.com/marketing/state-of-ai-report). AI can create impressive content, but editing remains crucial to ensure it aligns with brand voice and quality standards.

* Common applications of AI writing tools include emails & newsletters (47%), text-based social posts (46%), video-based social posts (46%), and long-form content and blogs (38%) ([HubSpot State of AI Report 2024)](https://blog.hubspot.com/marketing/state-of-ai-report).

* 64% of marketers have reported using AI tools to enhance their understanding of customers. The information gained from this exercise allows marketers to create materials that align with customer interests ([HubSpot State of AI Report 2024)](https://blog.hubspot.com/marketing/state-of-ai-report).

* Almost 65% of companies have seen better SEO results with AI tools ([Semrush AI Content Marketing Report 2024](https://www.semrush.com/contentshake/ai-content-marketing-report/)).

* AI implementation has led to noticeable benefits for organizations as 34.1% of marketers have reported a significant improvement in their marketing outcomes ([Influencer Marketing Hub AI Marketing Report 2024](https://influencermarketinghub.com/ai-marketing-benchmark-report/)). Check out [Typeface customer stories](/resources#customer-stories) to find some remarkable outcomes several Fortune 500 brands have achieved with Typeface’s AI capabilities.

* According to 42.2% of marketers in a survey, generative AI tools have transformed marketing strategies by improving content creation and campaign efficiency ([Influencer Marketing Hub AI Marketing Report 2024](https://influencermarketinghub.com/ai-marketing-benchmark-report/)).

### **2. Social media marketing statistics**

Social media remains one of the most important channels for building engagement and driving growth. But to stop the scroll, brands need to work harder than ever to grab attention with content that's both high-quality and genuinely creative.

Typeface’s generative AI social media tools can help here by crafting personalized and creative content for social media marketing campaigns. The platform offers AI templates for generating LinkedIn and X posts, content blend tools for repurposing content for social, and an Visual Inspiration Studio for generating custom visuals for social.

Staying informed about the latest social media marketing trends can give businesses a strategic edge, helping them refine their marketing strategies and connect more effectively with their audiences.

The statistics below will give you a solid foundation to build from:

* 87% of social media marketers believe that consumers will turn to social media more often than search engines to look for brands ([HubSpot Social Media Trends Report 2024](https://offers.hubspot.com/social-media-trends-report)).

* Social media use is still growing with over 62.6% of people worldwide now using these platforms. On average, people spend 2 hours and 20 minutes daily on social media ([Datareportal report](https://datareportal.com/reports/digital-2024-april-global-statshot)).

* The Gen Z population averages 2 hours and 51 minutes per day on social media, spending more time on these platforms than older generations. Nearly 30% of Gen Z turn to social media for inspiration ([GWI Social Media Trends Report 2024](https://www.gwi.com/reports/social)). Since Gen Z devotes more time to social media, it would be beneficial for marketers to focus on platforms that are most popular with this group. This could include TikTok, Instagram, and Snapchat.

* YouTube is now the top social media platform for brands with 79% growth over the past year, beating Instagram and Facebook. It's become a key place for consumer engagement ([HubSpot Social Media Trends Report 2024](https://offers.hubspot.com/social-media-trends-report)). Given YouTube's explosion in growth, focusing on creating engaging video content should be a top priority for brands in 2025.

* Among the biggest challenges for social media marketers are creating engaging content, finding new content ideas, and keeping up with feature and algorithm updates ([HubSpot Social Media Trends Report 2024](https://offers.hubspot.com/social-media-trends-report)). Generative AI tools can help address some of these issues by streamlining content creation and idea generation.

[Source](https://offers.hubspot.com/social-media-trends-report)

* The percentage of platform users in each region who reported using Facebook Marketplace or Instagram Shopping Bag: 39% in North America, 26% in Europe, 33% in the Middle East and Africa, 30% in Asia Pacific, and 42% in Latin America ([GWI Social Media Trends Report 2024](https://www.gwi.com/reports/social)). Social commerce is clearly on the rise globally as people increasingly turn to these platforms for their shopping needs. Collaborating with influencers who align with your brand can help reach their already engaged audiences.

* Latin American consumers are the top demographic engaging with social media ads and sponsored posts while consumers in North America lead in making in-app purchases ([GWI Social Media Trends Report 2024](https://www.gwi.com/reports/social)).

* For 86% of social media marketers, social search plays a crucial role in their overall content marketing strategy ([HubSpot Social Media Trends Report 2024](https://offers.hubspot.com/social-media-trends-report)). When developing your social media marketing plans, it might be a good idea to focus on optimizing your content for social SEO. This could involve using relevant hashtags, engaging captions, and creating content that resonates with what people are actively searching for.

* According to 68% of social media marketers, their companies invest in paid advertisements on social media platforms ([HubSpot Social Media Trends Report 2024](https://offers.hubspot.com/social-media-trends-report)).

* 71% of social media marketers incorporate AI tools into their social media strategies. The same percentage of marketers report that content created with generative AI outperformed content made without AI ([HubSpot Social Media Trends Report 2024](https://offers.hubspot.com/social-media-trends-report)).

* For 96% of social media marketers, ephemeral content like polls and Instagram stories delivers an average or high return on investment ([HubSpot Social Media Trends Report 2024](https://offers.hubspot.com/social-media-trends-report)).

* According to 86% of social media marketers, creating an active online community is essential for a successful social media marketing strategy in 2024 ([HubSpot Social Media Trends Report 2024](https://offers.hubspot.com/social-media-trends-report)).

### **3. Digital advertising statistics**

Digital advertising is reshaping how businesses and consumers interact on a global scale, and generative AI opens up a whole new level of possibilities.

With Typeface's AI capabilities, you can easily make Google display and search ads as well as social media ads. The AI tool summarizes your product's unique features from your URL and also helps design product images for ads with the [Visual Inspiration Studio](/product/ai-visual-inspiration-and-ideation).

Need to scale your campaigns? Typeface's [Ad Agent](/product/ad-agent) feature takes one parent ad and quickly adapts it into multiple variations with different aspect ratios, channels, and audience segments.

But the world of digital advertising moves fast. Trends shift, platforms update their algorithms, and consumer behavior evolves constantly. Staying informed about what's working is essential for maintaining your competitive edge.

Check out these statistics that might help shape your digital advertising strategies in 2025:

* Digital ad spending worldwide is projected to reach $740.3 billion by 2025 ([Oberlo](https://www.oberlo.com/statistics/digital-ad-spend)). As more money is poured into digital advertising, the competition will likely intensify. Brands will need to be more creative and strategic to stand out in the coming year.

* Facebook and Google continue to dominate US digital ad spending, capturing 19.9% and 38.6% of the market, respectively ([eMarketer](https://www.emarketer.com/content/google-and-facebook-s-digital-dominance-fading-as-rivals-share-grows)). Investing in ads on these platforms can help businesses tap into their vast user bases and advanced targeting capabilities.

[Source](https://www.emarketer.com/content/google-and-facebook-s-digital-dominance-fading-as-rivals-share-grows)

* The average CTR for Google Ads is 3.17% (search network) and 0.46% (display network), across all industries ([WordStream Google Ads industry Benchmark Report](https://www.wordstream.com/resources/google-ads-industry-benchmarks)). If your CTRs are significantly below these averages, it might be time to tweak your advertising strategy in 2025. For search ads, make sure your keywords are relevant and compelling. For display ads, emphasizing eye-catching visuals could be key.

* The average CPC for Google Ads is 2.69% (search network) and 0.63% (display network), across all industries ([WordStream Google Ads Industry Benchmark Report](https://www.wordstream.com/resources/google-ads-industry-benchmarks)).

* You may already be aware that Google is gradually phasing out third-party cookies. As marketers search for alternatives to third-party cookie targeting, social media targeting has become a promising option. In fact, 25% are thinking about using targeted social media ads ([Hubspot State of Marketing Report 2024](https://www.hubspot.com/marketing-statistics)).

### **4. SEO content planning statistics**

Content marketing works best when you understand how it connects with SEO to boost your online visibility. Why this matters? Because [68% of online experiences start with a search engine](https://videos.brightedge.com/research-report/BrightEdge_ChannelReport2019_FINAL.pdf). With strategic SEO planning essential, you can improve the chances of your content being discovered by search engines but also attract the right audience to your website.

Typeface [AI SEO tools](/use-cases/seo-and-web-content) can make this easier by optimizing your content for SEO and your target audience, which helps drive more qualified traffic and leads to your site.

If you want to step up your SEO efforts, here are some statistics that you can use to refine your content marketing strategies and ensure content reaches the right audience effectively:

* A majority of B2B and B2C companies, specifically 83%, believe that AI will positively influence SEO ([Conductor State of Organic Marketing Report 2024](https://www.conductor.com/academy/state-of-organic-marketing/)).

* Google's algorithm relies on more than 200 factors to rank websites ([Backlinko](https://backlinko.com/google-ranking-factors)). For 2025 marketing strategies, there's a need to prioritize optimizing the website for a wide range of factors to improve Google ranking. It's important to ensure that everything from quality content to mobile-friendliness is up to par.

* Almost 93% of companies have stated that search engine optimization had a positive effect on their website performance and marketing objectives ([Conductor State of Organic Marketing Report 2024](https://www.conductor.com/academy/state-of-organic-marketing/)).

* On average, organic search results that appear on the first page of Google have 1,447 words ([Backlinko](https://backlinko.com/search-engine-ranking)). Writing detailed, high-quality content approximately 1500-2000 words long might help enhance your website’s likelihood of appearing on Google’s first page.

* Organizations with advanced SEO maturity were most likely to see a positive impact in their marketing efforts. In contrast, those with low SEO maturity were more likely to see a negative impact ([Conductor State of Organic Marketing Report 2024](https://www.conductor.com/academy/state-of-organic-marketing/)).

[Source](https://www.conductor.com/academy/state-of-organic-marketing/)

* A whopping 96.55% of the 340.8 billion pages in the Ahrefs index receive no traffic from Google ([Ahrefs Search Traffic Study](https://ahrefs.com/blog/search-traffic-study/)). There are a few potential reasons for this: topics without search demand, the page lacks backlinks, or it could fail to match the search intent.

* The top result on Google gets about 27.6% of all clicks ([Backlinko](https://backlinko.com/google-ctr-stats)). An [Ahrefs study](https://ahrefs.com/blog/search-traffic-study/) has also found that there is a positive relationship between the amount of traffic a page receives from searches and the number of websites linking to it. This underscores the importance of investing in SEO practices—especially focusing on quality content creation and link-building initiatives—to boost online visibility and attract more visitors.

* Google Ads Keyword Planner tends to overestimate keyword search volumes about 55% of the time while being reasonably accurate around 45% of the time ([Ahrefs](https://ahrefs.com/blog/gsc-gkp-search-volume-study/)). To get the most reliable results, it's a good idea to use several keyword research tools.

* Web pages that rank high typically load faster ([BrightEdge](https://www.brightedge.com/blog/seo-trends-2024-websites-are-getting-faster-smarter-and-more-user-friendly)). This could be due to better SEO strategies and Google's Page Experience update that favors pages with a better user experience.

* Keyword density, the total number of keywords in a content piece, and the word count on high-ranking pages have all decreased. However, the on-page SEO score has gone up ([BrightEdge](https://www.brightedge.com/blog/seo-trends-2024-websites-are-getting-faster-smarter-and-more-user-friendly)). This could mean that good SEO practices, like using meta tags and placing keywords in important places on the page, prove more useful in the long run.

### **5. AI in search** statistics

Google's AI Overviews (AIOs) have changed the search experience by providing detailed answers right on the search results page.

The recent launch of [AI Mode](https://blog.google/products/search/ai-mode-search/) takes this evolution further by employing a sophisticated "query fan-out" approach, breaking down searches into multiple sub-queries and gathering information from various sources to provide detailed answers.

This means your content strategy must evolve beyond simple keyword optimization to focus on being citation-worthy within AI-generated answers.

The impact on traditional SEO metrics is already evident. While Google reports increased search usage, publishers are seeing significant drops in click-through rates.

Success now depends on achieving visibility within AI responses rather than just securing top rankings. Your content needs to demonstrate deep topical authority with quantified data, cited sources, and comprehensive coverage of related concepts.

These changes require a fundamental rethinking of content strategy. To develop effective SEO strategies that work in an AI-driven search environment, you need to understand exactly how these changes are playing out. The statistics below show just how dramatically AI is reshaping the search experience and what it means for your content strategy.

* AI overviews appear for 9.46% of all keywords, with 43% of AI overviews pointing back to Google ([Ahrefs](https://ahrefs.com/blog/ai-marketing-statistics/)).
* Since the core update from March, AI overviews have seen a 116% increase ([Ahrefs](https://ahrefs.com/blog/ai-marketing-statistics/)).
* Brand mentions on the web have the highest correlation with brand visibility in AI Overviews ([Ahrefs](https://ahrefs.com/blog/ai-marketing-statistics/)).
* Websites that hold the top spot in Google search results (blue links) have 25% chances of being featured as a source in AI Overviews ([Ahrefs](https://ahrefs.com/blog/ai-marketing-statistics/)).
* AI contributes to 0.1% of the overall referral traffic ([Ahrefs](https://ahrefs.com/blog/ai-marketing-statistics/)).
* Since AIOs launched a year ago, search impressions on Google have risen by more than 49%, but click-through rates have dropped by almost 30% because users are getting more information directly from the AI Overview ([BrightEdge AI Overviews One Year Review 2025](https://videos.brightedge.com/assets/SGE-Guide/BrightEdge%20Report%20-%20AIO%20Overviews%20One%20Year%20Review%20Research%20Paper%20and%20Deep%20Dive%20.pdf)).

* Google now creates AI Overviews 7 times more often for searches with eight or more words than it did a year ago. This shows that AI Overviews have improved at handling complex, conversational questions and providing complete answers to detailed queries ([BrightEdge AI Overviews One Year Review 2025](https://videos.brightedge.com/assets/SGE-Guide/BrightEdge%20Report%20-%20AIO%20Overviews%20One%20Year%20Review%20Research%20Paper%20and%20Deep%20Dive%20.pdf)).

* AI Overviews now source 89% of their citations from URLs not in the top 10 search rankings. This shows that AIOs are sourcing content from deeper in the search results, rather than just top-ranking pages ([BrightEdge AI Overviews One Year Review 2025](https://videos.brightedge.com/assets/SGE-Guide/BrightEdge%20Report%20-%20AIO%20Overviews%20One%20Year%20Review%20Research%20Paper%20and%20Deep%20Dive%20.pdf)).

* AI Overviews usually appear on less competitive, low-cost keywords with low search volumes — almost 60% have less than 100 searches each month. This suggests that Google is focusing on queries that aren't very competitive in search results and don't generate much ad revenue ([Semrush AI Overviews Study 2025](https://videos.brightedge.com/assets/SGE-Guide/BrightEdge%20Report%20-%20AIO%20Overviews%20One%20Year%20Review%20Research%20Paper%20and%20Deep%20Dive%20.pdf)).

* AIOs only match the exact query 5.4% of the time, showing that AI tends to rephrase or combine information instead of repeating the input word for word. This means AI answers aim to offer context, meaning, or relevance rather than just matching keywords ([Semrush AI Overviews Study 2025](https://www.semrush.com/blog/semrush-ai-overviews-study/)).

* The SERP is changing in appearance as well, with AIOs now dominating the top part of the page ([BrightEdge AI Overviews One Year Review 2025](https://videos.brightedge.com/assets/SGE-Guide/BrightEdge%20Report%20-%20AIO%20Overviews%20One%20Year%20Review%20Research%20Paper%20and%20Deep%20Dive%20.pdf)).
* AI overviews frequently use lists to make information easy to skim and summarize. While 12% of AI overviews use ordered lists, 61% contain unordered lists ([SurferSEO AI Overviews Study](https://surferseo.com/blog/ai-overviews-study/)).

### **6. B2B content marketing statistics**

Staying competitive as a SaaS business means keeping up with the latest B2B content marketing trends. It's that simple.

As companies increasingly adopt content-driven strategies to engage and inform their audience, these B2B content marketing statistics will provide valuable insights into what works and what doesn't:

* Content marketing is one of the main areas of spending in B2B marketing budgets ([2024 Sagefrog B2B Marketing Mix Report](https://www.semrush.com/blog/semrush-ai-overviews-study/)). This goes to show that businesses are recognizing the value of creating engaging, informative content to connect with their target audiences. By investing in content marketing, companies can build trust, establish thought leadership, and nurture long-term relationships with both existing and potential customers.

* This year, the preferred strategy for B2B marketing was a blend of in-house and outsourced efforts, chosen by 49% of respondents. Meanwhile, 35% opted to keep marketing completely in-house, and 16% outsourced all their marketing activities. Interestingly, 89% of organizations that outsourced their content marketing reported finding it to be effective ([2024 Sagefrog B2B Marketing Mix Report](https://www.sagefrog.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/Sagefrog_2024-B2B-Marketing-Mix-Report.pdf)). This indicates that businesses are looking for flexibility and a balance that allows them to leverage both internal expertise and external skills.

* Most B2B organizations (76%) have someone or a team specifically for content marketing. However, more than half (54%) of those with a content marketing team say it is small, with just two to five members. The rise in the use of generative AI tools might explain why these teams remain small ([CMI B2B Content Marketing Trends Research 2024](https://contentmarketinginstitute.com/articles/b2b-content-marketing-trends-research/)).

* In the past, generating qualified leads primarily relied on organic search, SEM, and paid social. Now, email marketing has become one of the top sources of sales and marketing leads ([2024 Sagefrog B2B Marketing Mix Report](https://www.sagefrog.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/Sagefrog_2024-B2B-Marketing-Mix-Report.pdf)). One possible reason could be that with email marketing, you can send personalized and targeted content directly to someone’s inbox. Plus, improved automation tools make it easy to segment audiences and measure strategy success.

* The most common B2B marketing challenge, cited by 54% of marketers this year, is a lack of resources. Another ongoing challenge is aligning content with marketing and sales operations, with 43% identifying it as a challenge ([CMI B2B Content Marketing Trends Research 2024](https://contentmarketinginstitute.com/articles/b2b-content-marketing-trends-research/)). AI tools can help address the lack of resources in B2B marketing by automating content creation and providing personalized, data-driven insights, making it easier to align content with marketing and sales operations.

[Source](https://contentmarketinginstitute.com/articles/b2b-content-marketing-trends-research/)

* For 35% of B2B content marketers, SEO optimization is one of their biggest challenges. Surprisingly, only 27% of these marketers see creating quality content as a challenge ([CMI B2B Content Marketing Trends Research 2024](https://contentmarketinginstitute.com/articles/b2b-content-marketing-trends-research/)). Generative AI tools can help B2B content marketers address these challenges by efficiently optimizing content for SEO while simultaneously crafting high-quality material.

* B2B marketers are increasingly adopting AI for content creation ([2024 Sagefrog B2B Marketing Mix Report](https://www.sagefrog.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/Sagefrog_2024-B2B-Marketing-Mix-Report.pdf)). 81% of B2B marketers are using generative AI tools in 2024, up from 72% last year. More than 38% of marketers report that their organization has AI guidelines in place. ([CMI B2B Content Marketing Trends Research 2024](https://contentmarketinginstitute.com/articles/b2b-content-marketing-trends-research/)) AI adoption for content creation will most likely increase in 2025 as more companies recognize its potential benefits.

* 38% of marketers have technology but aren't using it to its full potential. This has increased from 30% last year ([CMI B2B Content Marketing Trends Research 2024](https://contentmarketinginstitute.com/articles/b2b-content-marketing-trends-research/)). The rapid evolution of marketing technologies and their complex integration into existing workflows often lead to underutilization or misalignment with business goals. For a successful 2025 marketing strategy, companies should focus on training, clear strategy and alignment, and establishing a feedback loop.

* Almost 45% of B2B marketers don't have a scalable model for content creation ([CMI B2B Content Marketing Trends Research 2024](https://contentmarketinginstitute.com/articles/b2b-content-marketing-trends-research/)). Creating engaging, informative content takes time and skill. If a company needs to produce a lot of content, it can be hard to keep standards high without a scalable system. Without the right tools or teamwork, businesses may struggle to meet demand while maintaining content quality.

* For 89% of B2B marketers, webinars are effective for building brand awareness and generating leads ([2024 Sagefrog B2B Marketing Mix Report](https://www.sagefrog.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/Sagefrog_2024-B2B-Marketing-Mix-Report.pdf)).

* B2B marketers use a variety of content types: 92% use short articles or posts, 69% use long articles, 75% use case studies, 76% use videos, 57% use visual content, and 51% use e-books or white papers ([CMI B2B Content Marketing Trends Research 2024](https://contentmarketinginstitute.com/articles/b2b-content-marketing-trends-research/)).

### **6. Video marketing statistics**

Video content has emerged as a powerful tool for marketers looking to engage and convert audiences effectively. With AI tools for video content generation, creating this content has become easier than ever.

AI tools can generate videos from simple text prompts and even create scripts for videos. Typeface provides an AI template to help you make TikTok video scripts from prompts. It also provides a video clip generator, allowing you to quickly search and find long-form videos and turn them into multiple short-form clips to get more mileage out of your existing videos.

But with brands fighting for attention in an endless scroll of information, understanding the impact and reach of video marketing becomes crucial.

Here are some video marketing statistics that highlight the growing importance of video as a central component in marketing strategies:

* The majority of businesses (93%) consider video to be a key component of their marketing strategy ([Wistia State of Video Report 2024](https://wistia.com/learn/marketing/video-marketing-statistics)).

* 85% of video marketers intend to keep their video spending the same or increase it ([Wyzowl](https://www.wyzowl.com/video-marketing-statistics/)).

* Small businesses make a video every 24 days, medium-sized businesses do so every 4 days, and large businesses create a video roughly every 3 days. This indicates that as businesses grow, they tend to produce videos more often ([Wistia State of Video Report 2024](https://wistia.com/learn/marketing/video-marketing-statistics)).

* Nearly 38% of video marketers use a combination of both external and in-house teams to produce their content ([Wyzowl](https://www.wyzowl.com/video-marketing-statistics/)).

* 75% of marketers report using AI tools to assist in creating or editing their marketing videos ([Wyzowl](https://www.wyzowl.com/video-marketing-statistics/)).

* Many businesses use video to generate leads, boost sales, educate people about their products, and encourage product adoption ([Wistia State of Video Report 2024](https://wistia.com/learn/marketing/video-marketing-statistics)).

* Most companies (67%) are creating videos mainly for their websites. Many of them have video galleries displaying product and training videos, webinar recordings, podcasts, original series, and more ([Wistia State of Video Report 2024](https://wistia.com/learn/marketing/video-marketing-statistics)).

[Source](https://wistia.com/learn/marketing/video-marketing-statistics)

* The most popular types of videos produced by businesses are product videos, educational videos, live events, and webinars ([Wistia State of Video Report 2024](https://wistia.com/learn/marketing/video-marketing-statistics)).

* Live-action videos are the most frequently produced type of video, with 48% of marketers primarily focusing on them. In second place are animated videos at 24%, followed by screen-recorded videos at 22% ([Wyzowl](https://www.wyzowl.com/video-marketing-statistics/)).

* In 2024, video testimonials were the top choice for marketers, with 39% having produced them. Other popular choices were - explainer videos at 38%, social media videos and presentation videos at 34% each, product demos at 32%, video ads at 30%, sales videos at 30%, teaser videos at 30%, customer service videos at 28%, videographics at 25%, employee onboarding videos at 25%, training videos at 22%, customer onboarding videos at 22% and app demos at 22% ([Wyzowl](https://www.wyzowl.com/video-marketing-statistics/)).

## What is AI in content marketing, and how does it work?

AI in content marketing refers to the use of AI technologies across various stages of your marketing strategy.

Since marketing is inherently multidisciplinary, there is no single, universally accepted definition of AI in marketing.

You can use AI to achieve unique goals within the marketing umbrella: AI for SEO vs. AI for personalization vs. AI for image generation.

Irrespective of your use of AI in content marketing, at the core, there are two foundational technologies: **machine learning** (ML) and **deep learning** (DL).

These two AI technologies power core applications such as:

* **Natural language processing** (NLP), which helps machines understand, interpret, and generate human language
* **Computer vision,** which processes and analyzes visual content, is valuable for image tagging, video analysis, and more
* **Voice and speech recognition** which uses deep learning-based acoustic models to transcribe, understand, and respond to spoken language

SaaS businesses bundle these applications into end-user solutions in content marketing, social media management, customer experience, and service platforms.

Some of the most popular AI solutions in content marketing are:

* **Generative AI** (such as large language models) that can produce human-like content, assist with ideation, and personalize communication
* **Predictive analytics**, built on top of ML/DL, analyze existing customer data and predict future outcomes such as who’ll churn, who’ll convert and recommends personalized content
* **Sentiment analysis** and **social listening** use NLP to analyze text, such as from Tweets, and classify them into negative, positive, neutral sentiments, and extract themes and topics automatically
* **Chatbots** and **conversational AI** that uses NLP to understand queries, interact with humans in their language, and provide helpful resources

You can choose AI solutions for your unique requirements based on your content marketing discipline.

Nevertheless, the ultimate impact and purpose of using AI in content marketing boil down to:

✅ Faster research and brainstorming process

✅ Accelerated content creation

✅ Improved personalization

✅ Better segmentation and targeting

✅ Deeper and more insightful data analytics

✅ Cost efficiency and resource optimization

Unlike [marketing automation](/cxm/marketing-automation/) which speeds up manual tasks, AI adds context to how you plan, create, deliver, and optimize content.

## 3. Digital marketers use AI tools for a range of processes and tasks

A [SurveyMonkey study](https://www.surveymonkey.com/mp/ai-marketing-statistics/) found that today’s tech-savvy marketing teams use AI tools for a mix of key tasks. Here’s a breakdown:

## 4. AI marketers face challenges over quality concerns (among others)

The same study from SurveyMonkey highlighted common challenges industry professionals face in relation to AI.

31% of marketers have concerns around the accuracy or quality of AI tools while others feel uncertain around strategic direction or performance expectations. Here’s a summary:

* 50% of marketers expect to see expectations around their performance to increase
* 49% of marketers and their teams expect to see changes to the tools and software they use
* 48% of marketers believe that they may see shifts in strategy or direction as a result of AI technology in the not so distant future

## 5. Some marketing pros are reluctant to use AI due to safety issues

[Salesforce](https://www.salesforce.com/news/stories/generative-ai-statistics/#:~:text=39%25%20of%20marketers%20don%E2%80%99t%20know%20how%20to%20use,important%20for%20successfully%20using%20it%20in%20their%20role.) reveals that some marketers are reluctant to embrace autonomous technology. To leverage AI in marketing and use it to drive sustainable results, training, learning, and knowledge sharing is key.

## 6. 75% of companies who use AI for marketing are expected to shift to more strategic activities

Despite reports in the media, many companies believe that AI has the potential to enhance existing jobs rather than steal them.

[Gartner’s recent AI in Marketing](https://www.gartner.com/en/marketing/topics/ai-in-marketing) report shows that 75% of companies currently investing in AI technology are looking to move their talent into more strategic roles this year and beyond.

As [AI tools can automate repetitive processes](https://digitalmarketinginstitute.com/blog/examples-of-ai-in-marketing-automation), the future looks bright for marketers looking to use their time for activities that require more creative or strategic thinking.

## 7. 69% of marketing professionals feel hopeful about AI technology and how it could shape their jobs

[69% of marketers feel excited](https://www.surveymonkey.com/resources/premium/marketing-trends-for-a-new-era/?ut_source=mp&ut_source2=ai-marketing-statistics&ut_source3=inline) about AI’s impact on their jobs. Based on the fact that many businesses are looking to elevate the scope of their employees’ existing roles (see stat number six)—there’s definitely a sense of optimism in the air.

While there’s definitely some concern about AI taking peoples’ jobs, it appears that most marketing professionals see its potential. Working in harmony with AI technology can improve output and enhance insight—the key is understanding how to use certain tools or platforms to your advantage.

## 8. Over half of marketing teams use AI tools to optimize content

Rather than using generative AI tools like [ChatGPT](https://digitalmarketinginstitute.com/resources/videos/walkthrough-get-started-with-chatgpt-basics) to whip up countless words on specific subjects, [51% of marketers](https://www.surveymonkey.com/resources/premium/marketing-trends-for-a-new-era/?ut_source=mp&ut_source2=ai-marketing-statistics&ut_source3=inline) use them to optimize content.

Whether enhancing new or existing content, many marketing professionals use AI tools to:

* Add relevant target keywords into text as naturally as possible
* Repurposing a piece of content for different platforms
* Reworking a piece of content to suit the needs of different audiences
* Requesting editorial feedback and guidance

These AI use cases highlight how AI tools can complement human efforts to streamline processes and improve marketing outcomes.

## 9. 65% of companies have seen better SEO results when using AI

According to longshot AI, [65% of businesses](https://www.semrush.com/news/288870-new-report-reveals-the-top-ai-content-and-seo-trends-for-2024/) have seen an improvement in their [SEO](https://digitalmarketinginstitute.com/blog/what-is-seo) outcomes as a result of working with AI tools.

As existing adopters become more proficient with AI marketing technologies, we expect to see improvements in audience segmentation and personalization.
